For the sideways movement, you simply press this button to activate the rear-wheel swiveling mechanism.

Then, you can move the stroller sideways.

Once you release the button, the stroller returns to its normal mode of movement.

Since this is a prototype, one side of the rear wheels isn't working as smoothly as intended. However, you can still see how the feature works.

Next, let me show you the rotating handlebar.

You press this button here, and then rotate the handlebar toward the center of the stroller.

As I mentioned earlier, this allows you to walk beside the stroller instead of always pushing it from behind.

This can give you a clearer view of traffic ahead while also helping you maneuver in tight spaces.

Now, let me show you how to fold the stroller.

The seat can fold in both forward-facing and parent-facing positions, so there's no need to change the seat direction before folding.

The folding process involves just three steps.

First, lower the handlebar to its lowest position.

Second, if the seat is forward-facing, flip the seat board so that it aligns with the handlebar.

You'll then find a folding bar underneath the seat.

Third, simply rotate the bar to release the folding mechanism. The stroller then folds down with the help of gravity.

Once it's folded, you can lift it up by holding the folding bar.

If the seat is parent-facing, you just need to align the backrest with the handlebar before following the same folding process.

And once folded, the stroller can stand on its own.

Now, let me show you how to unfold the stroller.

Unfolding is simply the reverse of the folding process.

Since the stroller can be carried directly by the folding bar, we haven't included a separate carry hook in the current design.

This means you don't need to press a release button to disengage the hook before unfolding. You can simply open the stroller directly.

However, if you would prefer to have a carry hook, we can certainly add one based on your preference.

Closing

So, that's the main idea behind Nimble.

It's designed to give parents more flexibility in how they move, maneuver, fold, and carry the stroller.

I'd be happy to answer any questions before we move on to our next stroller.
